new_statements.rule_in_words: Gepo (Luquan Gepu) is described as a syllable-tone language with three basic level/falling tones 55, 33, 21 plus a sandhi tone 44 (<33) and a marginal 24; the source gives segment and tone inventories only and says nothing about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Tone 44 arises by sandhi from 33; tone 24 attested in a single disyllabic word (treated as sandhi).
new_statements.domain_note: Tone is lexical per syllable; no statement about word- or phrase-level prominence. Data are the author's own 2003 elicitation from one Luquan speaker (Su Wenliang, 44, Luquan Ethnicity Bureau).
new_statements.identity_note: Lama 2012's datapoint is 'Gepu 葛濮 (Luquan)' [ko33phu44], Luquan County — Glottolog 5.1 equates it with Kophu = Gepo [ygp] (gepo1234, Nasu-Gepu subgroup, which is itself based on Lama 2012). Jiang 2022 describes Gepo 葛颇 ko44(pʰu21) of Xiaozhiyi, Luxi County (she calls it a southeastern-dialect Yi variety); Li Shengfu 2007 describes Epo 峨颇 ŋo33phu21 of Longlin, Guangxi; Li Dejun 2011 describes Alingpo of Yimeidu, Shilin — all filed under gepo1234 by Glottolog but they are geographically distinct varieties and may differ in tone systems. Katie Gao 2017's 'Geipo' (Wuding, Central Ngwi) is explicitly NOT this language.

sources.note: Short first-hand phonological profile of Gepu 葛濮 (Luquan) [ko33phu44] from the author's own 2003 elicitation (consultant Su Wenliang, Luquan): 42 initials, 18 monophthong vowels, 4 tones 55 (44) 33 21, 44 = sandhi of 33, marginal 24 in one disyllable (p.77; Table 4.18 fn.55 p.107). Nothing anywhere in the dissertation about stress/accent (a full-text search for stress/accent: no hits).
